system_description.narrative_title: U.S.-Iran standoff at the Strait of Hormuz: blockade and economic pressure
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapidly intensifying US–Iran confrontation centered on control of the Strait of Hormuz is being waged through a mix of naval deployments, unilateral blockades and unprecedented economic measures, producing immediate disruptions to shipping and global energy markets. The situation functions as an open system: actions by state actors (military maneuvers, economic tactics, claims of control) produce feedbacks through oil prices, trade flows, regional alignments and domestic political pressures, which in turn influence subsequent military and economic policy choices. Secondary actors (Gulf states, shipping firms, markets, BRICS partners) both respond to and reshape the trajectory, creating cascading economic and security effects beyond the immediate theater.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: US and Iranian policy actions (naval deployments, blockades, economic sanctions/tactics), incidents in the Strait of Hormuz (attacks on vessels, claims of control), regional state and proxy responses (UAE, Saudi, Houthis, Iran-aligned forces), global oil flows and prices, shipping traffic and insurance, market impacts (stocks, mortgage and fuel costs), and public/political messaging (US administration rhetoric, Iranian leadership signals).
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical-economic system (international security architecture intertwined with global energy, trade and finance networks).
adjacent_subsystems: Gulf regional security architecture (GCC, UAE, Saudi, Iran proxies)
Global shipping, logistics and maritime insurance networks
Domestic politics and defense-industrial posture in the US and partners
evidence_headlines: U.S. to use economic tactics on Iran `that have never been seen'; Navy works to relieve troubled carrier Abraham Lincoln
US can keep naval blockade on Iranian ports "indefinitely," Pentagon chief says
Iran, US make competing claims over control of Strait of Hormuz
UAE's ADNOC says one of its vessels came under attack while transiting Hormuz
Oil steadies after US threatens to blockade Iran indefinitely
Trump urges Americans to accept higher gas prices as he escalates Iran rhetoric - reuters.com

variables.name: Naval deployment density
variables.description: The concentration of military naval assets and operational patrols deployed in and around the maritime choke point measured per unit area/time.

variables.name: Maritime transit rate
variables.description: The volume of commercial vessel transits through the choke point per unit time.

variables.name: Oil flow through choke point
variables.description: The throughput of crude and refined petroleum products transiting the choke point measured in barrels per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of hostile or disruptive incidents affecting ships (attacks, interdictions, boardings, near misses) in the maritime corridor per unit time.

variables.name: Blockade effectiveness
variables.description: The degree to which interdiction measures reduce the ability of vessels and cargo to transit the targeted ports and waterways.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: The average premium charged for war, hull and transit insurance for vessels operating in the affected maritime area.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: The market price level of benchmark crude oil reflecting current supply-demand expectations.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: The short-term variability and uncertainty in energy commodity prices and trading conditions.

variables.name: Trade rerouting cost
variables.description: The additional transport and time-costs incurred when commercial trade is rerouted around the disrupted corridor.

variables.name: Proxy activity intensity
variables.description: The scale and intensity of operations by non-state or irregular actors conducting maritime or regional actions linked to the confrontation.

variables.name: Economic pressure intensity
variables.description: The overall magnitude of unilateral and multilateral economic measures applied to coerce policy change, measured by trade/financial restrictions and targeted measures.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: The level of public opinion, media scrutiny and political demands within governments that constrain or push for policy actions related to the confrontation.

variables.name: Allied cooperation strength
variables.description: The degree of coordinated operational, diplomatic and economic action among external partner actors influencing the confrontation.

variables.name: Vessel compliance rate
variables.description: The proportion of commercial vessels adhering to navigational advisories, blockade directives or alternate routing guidance.

variables.name: Global fuel supply gap
variables.description: The difference between global liquid fuel supply and demand that determines market tightness and vulnerability to disruptions.

variables.name: Market contagion intensity
variables.description: The extent to which financial and commodity market stress from the confrontation spreads across asset classes and geographies.

catalysts.title: U.S. maintains/extends naval blockade
catalysts.description: Sustained U.S. claim it can keep a blockade 'indefinitely' and vows more economic pressure, implying continued enforcement of maritime interdictions.
catalysts.rationale: 'U.S. said it can keep naval blockade on Iran "indefinitely"'; US vows more economic pressure.

catalysts.title: Arrival/deployment of fresh U.S. carrier
catalysts.description: A newly dispatched U.S. aircraft carrier moves into the region to reinforce operations, increasing immediate naval presence and enforcement capability.
catalysts.rationale: 'U.S. Sending Fresh Aircraft Carrier to Middle East Amid Iran War Strain'; reinforces regional deployments.

catalysts.title: USS Abraham Lincoln rotation/return
catalysts.description: The Abraham Lincoln carrier group prepares to return home or rotate out, temporarily reducing deployed carrier presence and enforcement capacity.
catalysts.rationale: 'Iran war commander visits the USS Abraham Lincoln as carrier prepares to return home' — implies imminent rotation.

catalysts.title: U.S. escalates economic measures on Iran
catalysts.description: Washington rolls out new, unprecedented economic tactics and pledges stepped-up pressure aimed at coercing Iran economically and diplomatically.
catalysts.rationale: 'U.S. to use economic tactics on Iran "that have never been seen"' and 'Trump wants more economic pressure on Iran.'

catalysts.title: Sustained maritime attacks in Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Repeated attacks on commercial vessels and energy infrastructure continue, raising the frequency and geographic spread of maritime hostilities.
catalysts.rationale: 'two more ships attacked in Hormuz'; 'ADNOC vessel attacked in Hormuz'; repeated recent strikes reported.

catalysts.title: Stalled Hormuz negotiations continue
catalysts.description: Talks to resolve transit and blockade disputes remain stalled, prolonging uncertainty and a 'new normal' acceptance among Gulf states.
catalysts.rationale: 'Hormuz remains blocked' and 'stalled Hormuz talks' indicate continued negotiation impasse.

catalysts.title: Asian refiners buy more U.S. crude
catalysts.description: Refiners in Asia increase purchases of U.S. crude to compensate for disruption through Hormuz, shifting trade flows and supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: 'Asian refiners buy more US crude as Hormuz remains blocked,' traders say — shifting flows and costs.
